newsitem.title: UK: Dollar gains pared for now, US/Euro shares up.
newsitem.headline: Dollar gains pared for now, US/Euro shares up.

text.p: The dollar flexed its muscles again on Wednesday, although a scolding by the German Bundesbank sent it down from its highs.

The bank's verbal intervention curbed a steep dollar rise against the mark, countering a news agency report that Germany was keen on an even stronger U.S. currency to take some pressure off its economy.
But market analysts expected a renewed surge in the dollar in due course.
"I think we've seen the highs for the day but I doubt we've even seen the highs for the week," said Peter von Maydell, senior currency economist at UBS.
European bourses, meanwhile, took their cue from Wall Street to move ahead, although they had pared earlier gains by mid-afternoon. The New York market opened in upbeat mood to add to Tuesday's rise.
While ending below an earlier record high, Germany's 30-share DAX index still finished bourse trade at a record closing level, boosted by the dollar's strength, good news for German exporters.
But a bigger-than-forecast drop in the British jobless total rekindled fears of higher interest rates and sent the London stock market, Europe's busiest, lower before some revival in the afternoon.
On the bullion market, gold slipped to its lowest fix since April 1993 at $336.90 an ounce in the morning before recovering somewhat later.
A surge in the dollar to 34-month highs against the mark and four-year highs against the yen had prompted selling by both gold producers and long-term investors fearing still lower prices.

As the U.S. currency rose sharply against the mark, Swiss franc and yen in early business, currency traders reported market concern that central banks might soon step in to the market to cool things off.
The dollar surged to 1.6935 marks, 1.4500 Swiss francs and 124.48 yen, well up from Tuesday's late European levels of 1.6720, 1.4340 and 122.90.
In the event the Bundesbank succeeded in weakening the dollar for the time being with tough talking, saying it did not believe it should keep climbing, rather than actual market operations.

A report from the MNSI news agency had said Germany would welcome further dollar strength but the central bank said it continued to support the view of the Group of Seven leading industrial nations that the dollar's level had already corrected.
"That (G7) statement said the dollar has been corrected and it was made at a rate of 1.65 marks," the Bundesbank said.

Currency traders said Wednesday's second leg of the U.S. Treasury's quarterly refunding could give the dollar more support. Further ahead market players are looking to Thursday's U.S. January retail sales data and Friday's producer prices.
More signs of strength in the world's biggest economy could reignite the dollar's rally, contrasting with problems in Germany and Japan, analysts said.

The London stock market, already wary over the impact on companies of a strong pound, lost initial gains after news that unemployment fell 67,800 in January, more than double what economists had expected. Bonds also slipped.

"The labour market data are strong and while very unlikely to prompt a near-term tightening of policy, they will increase speculation that rates will have to rise immediately after the election," said Jeremy Hawkins, economist at Bank of America.
The strong dollar helped pushed sterling to fresh 52-month highs around 2.7685 marks, versus 2.7480 overnight, before it eased back near to 2.75.

Four years after being ejected from Europes exchange rate mechanism, the pound has almost climbed back to where it was -- giving the government ammunition to fight off an interest rate rise before an imminent election.
The Bank of England on Wednesday softened its call for higher interest rates, while Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke disagreed that rates needed to rise in the near term.
French shares, like those in Germany, benefited from the dollar's strength but were off their highs after the Bundesbank's remarks.
In New York, the Dow Jones industrial average was up around 25 points at 6,883 after an hour of trading to add to Tuesday's gain of 51.57 points.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6850 marks and 123.85 yen versus with 1.6720 and 122.90 late on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1530 GMT
London's FTSE-100 index was up 0.6 at 4,304.9.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX hit a record 3,228.58 before ending floor trade at a new closing high of 3,216.14, up 28.56. In Paris, the CAC-40 was 15.69 higher at 2,597.78.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold was fixed at $337.70 in the afternoon, up from its morning fix of $336.90 but still well below Tuesday's London close of $339.55. Silver slid to $4.86 from $4.93 but fellow precious metal palladium was fixed at $136.65, its highest since April 1996.
